events.title: The stone circles of Gobekli Tepe
events.description: Hunter-gatherers raise carved T-shaped pillars on a hilltop near Sanliurfa, thousands of years before pottery or farming. It overturned the assumption that monuments come after agriculture.

events.title: Wheat is domesticated in the Karacadag hills
events.description: Genetic studies trace einkorn wheat to the volcanic hills of southeastern Anatolia. The region is part of the arc where farming begins.

events.title: Catalhoyuk, a town without streets
events.description: Several thousand people live in packed mud-brick houses entered through the roof, with plastered bulls' heads on the walls and the dead buried under the floors.

events.title: Troy is founded
events.description: A fortified settlement at the mouth of the Dardanelles is rebuilt nine times over three thousand years. One of its layers is the city Homer's audience imagined.

events.title: Assyrian merchants at Kanesh
events.description: Traders from Ashur run a tin and textile business from a quarter of Kanesh, leaving some 23,000 clay tablets of letters, contracts and family quarrels. They are the oldest written records in Anatolia.

events.title: The Hittite kingdom at Hattusa
events.description: Hattusili I makes Hattusa his capital and the Hittites become the dominant power of Anatolia, writing the oldest attested Indo-European language.

events.title: The Hittites sack Babylon
events.description: Mursili I marches a thousand kilometres south and ends the dynasty of Hammurabi, then goes home without trying to hold the city.

events.title: The battle of Kadesh
events.description: Hittite and Egyptian chariot armies fight to a draw on the Orontes. Both kings claim victory in monumental inscriptions.

events.title: The first surviving peace treaty
events.description: Hattusili III and Ramesses II agree mutual defence and the return of fugitives. Copies survive in both languages, and a replica hangs at the United Nations.

events.title: The Hittite collapse
events.description: Hattusa is abandoned during the wider Bronze Age collapse. Famine, raiders and internal revolt all play a part and nobody is sure in what proportion.

events.title: Neo-Hittite city states
events.description: Hittite traditions survive in small kingdoms in the southeast such as Carchemish and Malatya, still carving in Luwian hieroglyphs.

events.title: Greeks settle the Aegean coast
events.description: Aeolian and Ionian settlers found cities along the western shore. Ionia becomes the most advanced part of the Greek world for four centuries.

events.title: The kingdom of Urartu at Lake Van
events.description: A highland kingdom builds fortresses, irrigation canals and wine cellars on the rock around Van, and rivals Assyria for two centuries.

events.title: Midas rules Phrygia from Gordion
events.description: A real king behind the legend of the golden touch rules central Anatolia. His city held the knot Alexander would later cut.

events.title: Homer composes in Ionia
events.description: The Iliad and the Odyssey take their final form in the eastern Aegean, probably around Smyrna or Chios. The war they describe is fought outside an Anatolian city.

events.title: Lydia strikes the first coins
events.description: Electrum pieces stamped with a lion's head are minted at Sardis. A state guarantees the weight of a lump of metal, and money as we use it begins.

events.title: Thales and the eclipse
events.description: Thales of Miletus is said to have predicted a solar eclipse that halts a battle between Lydia and Media. Ionian philosophy begins asking what the world is made of without asking the gods.

events.title: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus
events.description: Croesus pays for the columns of a temple counted among the Seven Wonders. It burns in 356 BCE on the night, the story goes, that Alexander is born.

events.title: Cyrus takes Sardis
events.description: Croesus, richest king in the world, loses his kingdom to Persia. All of Anatolia becomes Persian satrapies for two centuries.

events.title: The Ionian revolt
events.description: The Greek cities of the coast rise against Persia with Athenian help. Its suppression and the burning of Miletus lead directly to the Persian invasions of Greece.

events.title: Herodotus is born at Halicarnassus
events.description: The first historian to ask why things happened, and to go and ask the people involved, grows up in a Carian city under Persian rule.

events.title: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
events.description: A tomb for the satrap Mausolus becomes so famous that its name becomes the word for any grand tomb.

events.title: Alexander crosses at the Granicus
events.description: Alexander lands in Anatolia, wins his first battle against the Persian satraps, and cuts the Gordian knot the following winter.

events.title: The battle of Issus
events.description: At the edge of the Mediterranean in the southeast, Alexander routs Darius III and captures his family. Persian rule in Anatolia is over.

events.title: The battle of Ipsus divides the empire
events.description: Alexander's successors fight over his conquests. Anatolia is split among Seleucids, Ptolemies and a crowd of smaller kingdoms.

events.title: The Galatians arrive
events.description: Celtic bands hired as mercenaries settle around modern Ankara. The Galatia of Paul's letter is theirs.

events.title: Pergamon and its library
events.description: The Attalid kings build a library to rival Alexandria and, when Egypt cuts off papyrus, develop the prepared skins the world calls parchment after the city.

events.title: Pergamon is bequeathed to Rome
events.description: Attalus III dies and leaves his kingdom to the Roman people in his will. It becomes the province of Asia, the richest Rome owns.

events.title: Mithridates and the Asiatic Vespers
events.description: The king of Pontus orders every Roman and Italian in Anatolia killed on one day. Tens of thousands die and Rome spends twenty-five years fighting him.

events.title: Veni, vidi, vici at Zela
events.description: Caesar beats Pharnaces of Pontus in a five-day campaign and sums it up to the Senate in three words.

events.title: Paul's journeys through Anatolia
events.description: Paul of Tarsus preaches in the cities of Galatia and Asia. Most of the churches his letters are addressed to are in modern Turkey.

events.title: The seven churches of Revelation
events.description: The Book of Revelation is addressed to seven congregations in the province of Asia, from Ephesus to Laodicea.

events.title: Ephesus at its height
events.description: The provincial capital has perhaps two hundred thousand people. The Library of Celsus is finished within a few years.

events.title: An emperor captured at Edessa
events.description: Valerian is defeated and taken prisoner by the Persian king Shapur I near modern Sanliurfa, the only Roman emperor to die in enemy hands.

events.title: The Council of Nicaea
events.description: Constantine summons the bishops to Nicaea, modern Iznik, to settle whether Christ is equal to the Father. The creed they write is still recited every Sunday.

events.title: Constantinople is dedicated
events.description: Constantine refounds Byzantium as a new Christian capital on the Bosphorus. It is the seat of empire for the next sixteen centuries.

events.title: The empire divides for good
events.description: Theodosius dies and the empire is split between his sons. The eastern half, governed from Constantinople, outlives the western by nearly a thousand years.

events.title: The Theodosian Walls
events.description: A triple land wall six kilometres long closes the peninsula. It holds against every attacker for a thousand years until gunpowder.

events.title: The Council of Chalcedon
events.description: A council across the water from the capital defines Christ as one person in two natures. The churches of Egypt, Syria and Armenia reject it and split away.

events.title: The Nika riots
events.description: Chariot-racing factions burn half the city and nearly topple Justinian. Theodora talks him out of fleeing and about thirty thousand are killed in the Hippodrome.

events.title: Hagia Sophia is consecrated
events.description: Built in under six years, its dome is the largest enclosed space in the world for a thousand years. It is cathedral, mosque, museum and mosque again.

events.title: The plague of Justinian
events.description: Bubonic plague reaches Constantinople by grain ship from Egypt and kills perhaps a third of the city in months. It returns for two centuries.

events.title: Greek fire breaks the Arab siege
events.description: A liquid incendiary pumped from ships burns the Umayyad fleet. Its recipe was a state secret so well kept it is still not known.

events.title: Iconoclasm
events.description: Leo III begins a campaign against religious images that splits the empire for over a century, and is finally reversed in 843.

events.title: The Great Schism
events.description: Papal legates excommunicate the Patriarch of Constantinople at the altar of Hagia Sophia, and he returns the favour. The two churches stay apart.

events.title: The battle of Manzikert
events.description: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeats and captures Emperor Romanos IV. Anatolia is opened to Turkish settlement and the date is still celebrated in Turkey.

events.title: The Sultanate of Rum
events.description: A branch of the Seljuks founds a state in Anatolia, calling it Rum after the Romans whose land it takes. Konya becomes its capital.

events.title: The First Crusade crosses Anatolia
events.description: Crusaders take Nicaea and win at Dorylaeum. The Byzantines recover the western coast while the Turks keep the plateau.

events.title: The battle of Myriokephalon
events.description: Kilij Arslan II ambushes the Byzantine army in a mountain pass. The emperor compares it to Manzikert, and the hope of retaking the interior dies.

events.title: The Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
events.description: A crusade diverted by Venetian debt storms the Christian capital and loots it for three days. The bronze horses on St Mark's in Venice came from the Hippodrome.

events.title: The caravanserai network
events.description: The Seljuks build fortified inns a day's ride apart along the trade roads, with free lodging for three days. Many still stand, such as the Sultan Han near Aksaray.

events.title: The Mongols win at Kose Dag
events.description: A Mongol army breaks the Seljuks in a single day. The sultanate survives as a tributary and Anatolia fractures into small Turkish principalities.

events.title: The Byzantines retake their capital
events.description: Michael VIII recovers Constantinople from the Latins. The restored empire is small, poor and surrounded.

events.title: Rumi dies at Konya
events.description: The Persian poet Jalal al-Din Rumi dies, and his followers found the order of whirling dervishes. He is one of the best-selling poets in the United States.

events.title: Osman founds a principality
events.description: A frontier chief at Sogut, on the Byzantine border, begins the dynasty that will rule for six hundred years and gives it its name.

events.title: Bursa becomes the first Ottoman capital
events.description: Orhan takes the city after a long siege. The dynasty's early tombs are there.

events.title: The Ottomans cross into Europe
events.description: An earthquake brings down the walls of Gallipoli and Ottoman troops occupy it. The state's centre of gravity moves into the Balkans.

events.title: Edirne becomes the capital
events.description: Adrianople, renamed Edirne, is the capital for ninety years. The Janissary corps of converted Christian boys is organised in the same period.

events.title: The battle of Kosovo
events.description: Ottoman forces defeat a Serbian coalition, but Sultan Murad I is killed on the field, the only sultan to die in battle.

events.title: Timur captures Bayezid at Ankara
events.description: Timur crushes the Ottoman army and takes the sultan prisoner. A decade of civil war among his sons follows, and the state nearly dies.

events.title: The fall of Constantinople
events.description: Mehmed II takes the city after a fifty-three-day siege with cannon cast by a Hungarian engineer. The last emperor dies on the walls and the Roman Empire ends.

events.title: Topkapi Palace begun
events.description: Mehmed starts the palace that will house the government and the sultan's household for four centuries.

events.title: Sephardic Jews welcomed
events.description: Bayezid II invites the Jews expelled from Spain to settle in the empire. Salonica becomes a majority-Jewish city.

events.title: The battle of Chaldiran
events.description: Selim I's artillery and Janissaries defeat the Safavid cavalry. The frontier between Ottoman and Persian lands settles roughly where the Turkish-Iranian border is today.

events.title: Selim conquers Egypt and takes the caliphate
events.description: The Mamluk sultanate falls, and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina come under the Ottomans. The sultans now claim to lead the Muslim world.

events.title: The battle of Mohacs
events.description: Suleiman destroys the Hungarian army in two hours and the king drowns in the retreat. Most of Hungary is Ottoman for a hundred and fifty years.

events.title: The first siege of Vienna
events.description: Suleiman reaches the Habsburg capital, but autumn rain and supply lines force him to withdraw. It marks the limit of Ottoman Europe.

events.title: Barbarossa wins at Preveza
events.description: The Ottoman admiral Hayreddin beats a Holy League fleet, and the eastern Mediterranean is an Ottoman sea for a generation.

events.title: The Suleymaniye Mosque
events.description: Sinan, the empire's chief architect, finishes the great mosque complex above the Golden Horn. He designs over three hundred buildings in his career.

events.title: Defeat at Lepanto
events.description: A Holy League fleet destroys the Ottoman navy off Greece. The fleet is rebuilt within a year, and Cyprus, taken that summer, stays Ottoman.

events.title: The Blue Mosque
events.description: Ahmed I begins the Sultan Ahmed Mosque facing Hagia Sophia, its six minarets a statement nobody else is allowed to match.

events.title: The Janissaries murder a sultan
events.description: Osman II tries to reform the army and is strangled by it. It is the first regicide in the dynasty and the soldiers' power over the throne is now plain.

events.title: The Koprulu viziers
events.description: A dynasty of grand viziers restores order, finances and the army for half a century, and the empire reaches its greatest extent.

events.title: Defeat at Vienna
events.description: A second siege of Vienna is broken by a Polish relief army. The long retreat from central Europe begins.

events.title: The treaty of Karlowitz
events.description: The Ottomans cede Hungary and much else. It is the first major treaty the empire signs as the loser.

events.title: The Tulip Period
events.description: Two decades of peace, garden parties and tulip mania at court. Westward curiosity grows and the first Ottoman printing press opens in 1727.

events.title: The treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca
events.description: Russia wins Crimea's independence and a claim to protect the sultan's Orthodox subjects. It is the opening of the Eastern Question.

events.title: Selim III's New Order
events.description: Selim builds a European-style army alongside the Janissaries. They depose and kill him for it in 1808.

events.title: The Auspicious Incident
events.description: Mahmud II provokes a Janissary revolt and destroys the corps with artillery in Istanbul. Several thousand are killed and reform can finally proceed.

events.title: Navarino and Greek independence
events.description: British, French and Russian ships destroy the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet. Greece is independent within five years, the first nation to leave the empire.

events.title: The Tanzimat edict
events.description: The Rose Garden decree promises security of life and property and equality before the law for all subjects. Four decades of legal and administrative reform follow.

events.title: The Crimean War
events.description: Britain and France fight beside the Ottomans against Russia. Florence Nightingale runs her hospital at Scutari across the Bosphorus.

events.title: The Reform Edict
events.description: Muslims and non-Muslims are declared equal. Many Muslims resent it and many Christians do not believe it.

events.title: Circassians arrive in exile
events.description: Hundreds of thousands of Muslims driven from the Caucasus by Russia land on the Black Sea coast, many dying in the camps.

events.title: The empire goes bankrupt
events.description: The state defaults on its foreign loans. A European-run debt administration later takes over whole branches of revenue.

events.title: The first constitution
events.description: Abdulhamid II proclaims a constitution and a parliament, then suspends both within two years and rules alone for three decades.

events.title: The Congress of Berlin
events.description: After defeat by Russia the empire loses most of its Balkan provinces. Another wave of Muslim refugees arrives in Anatolia.

events.title: The Hamidian massacres
events.description: Between 1894 and 1896 irregular troops and mobs kill perhaps a hundred thousand Armenians across eastern Anatolia.

events.title: The Young Turk revolution
events.description: Officers of the Committee of Union and Progress force the sultan to restore the constitution. A year later they depose him.

events.title: The Balkan Wars
events.description: In two years the empire loses almost all its European territory, including Salonica, the birthplace of Mustafa Kemal.

events.title: War on the German side
events.description: The Ottoman government enters the First World War. Enver Pasha's winter offensive at Sarikamis loses most of an army to the cold.

events.title: The Armenian genocide
events.description: Armenian community leaders are arrested in Istanbul, and deportations and massacres follow across Anatolia. Somewhere between 600,000 and 1.5 million Armenians die. The Turkish state disputes the term.

events.title: Gallipoli
events.description: British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops land on the peninsula and are held for eight months. A divisional commander named Mustafa Kemal makes his name there.

events.title: Mustafa Kemal lands at Samsun
events.description: Sent to disband the remaining troops, he organises resistance instead. The date is a national holiday.

events.title: The treaty of Sevres
events.description: The sultan's government signs away most of Anatolia to Greece, Armenia, France, Italy and a Kurdish state. It is never ratified, and Turks still speak of the Sevres syndrome.

events.title: The battle of Sakarya
events.description: Twenty-two days of fighting stop the Greek advance on Ankara. The national assembly gives Kemal the title Gazi.

events.title: The burning of Smyrna
events.description: Turkish forces retake Izmir and fire destroys the Greek and Armenian quarters. Tens of thousands die and hundreds of thousands flee by sea.

events.title: The sultanate is abolished
events.description: The Grand National Assembly ends six centuries of Ottoman rule. The last sultan leaves on a British warship.

events.title: The treaty of Lausanne
events.description: The Allies recognise Turkey's borders, and a population exchange sends about 1.2 million Orthodox Christians to Greece and 400,000 Muslims the other way.

events.title: The Republic is proclaimed
events.description: Turkey becomes a republic with Ankara as its capital and Mustafa Kemal as president.

events.title: The caliphate is abolished
events.description: The office the sultans had held since 1517 is ended and the dynasty exiled. Religious courts and schools close.

events.title: The Sheikh Said rebellion
events.description: A Kurdish and religious rising in the southeast is crushed and its leader hanged. The government takes emergency powers and closes the opposition.

events.title: The hat law
events.description: The fez is banned and brimmed hats required for men. Dervish lodges are shut the same year.

events.title: A Swiss civil code
events.description: Islamic family law is replaced with an adaptation of the Swiss code. Polygamy is banned and women gain equal rights in divorce and inheritance.

events.title: The alphabet changes overnight
events.description: Arabic script is replaced with a Latin alphabet, and Kemal tours the country with a blackboard teaching it. Within a generation almost nobody can read the Ottoman archives.

events.title: Surnames, and votes for women
events.description: Every citizen must take a surname, and the assembly gives Kemal his: Ataturk, father of the Turks. Women get the vote in national elections the same year.

events.title: Ataturk dies
events.description: He dies at Dolmabahce Palace in Istanbul at 9.05 in the morning. Sirens still sound at that minute every year and the country stops.

events.title: Hatay joins Turkey
events.description: The province of Alexandretta, under the French mandate in Syria, votes to join Turkey after a disputed referendum. Syria does not recognise it for decades.

events.title: The first free election
events.description: The Democrat Party of Adnan Menderes wins in a landslide and Ataturk's party hands over power peacefully.

events.title: Turkey joins NATO
events.description: After sending a brigade to Korea, Turkey enters the alliance and becomes its eastern flank against the Soviet Union.

events.title: The Istanbul pogrom
events.description: A false rumour about Ataturk's birthplace sets off two days of riots against Greek property. Most of Istanbul's Greek community leaves within a generation.

events.title: The first military coup
events.description: Officers overthrow Menderes, who is tried and hanged. It sets a pattern of the army stepping in to correct elected governments.

events.title: Workers go to Germany
events.description: A labour agreement with West Germany sends hundreds of thousands of Turkish workers north. About three million people of Turkish origin live in Germany today.

events.title: The first Bosphorus Bridge
events.description: Europe and Asia are joined by road for the first time, on the republic's fiftieth anniversary.

events.title: The invasion of Cyprus
events.description: After a Greek-backed coup on the island, Turkish troops land and take the north. Cyprus is still divided.

events.title: The 1980 coup
events.description: After years of street violence between left and right, the army takes over, arrests hundreds of thousands and writes a new constitution.

events.title: The PKK insurgency begins
events.description: The Kurdistan Workers' Party attacks army posts in the southeast. Some forty thousand people die over the following decades.

events.title: An application to join Europe
events.description: Turkey applies for membership of the European Community. It becomes a candidate in 1999 and talks have been frozen since 2018.

events.title: The Izmit earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake kills over seventeen thousand people in the industrial northwest. Greek rescuers arrive the next day and relations thaw.

events.title: Financial crisis
events.description: The lira collapses and the economy shrinks by a twentieth. The reform programme that follows underpins a decade of growth.

events.title: The AKP comes to power
events.description: Recep Tayyip Erdogan's new party wins a majority. He leads the country as prime minister and then president from then on.

events.title: Orhan Pamuk's Nobel
events.description: The novelist wins the Nobel Prize in Literature a year after being prosecuted for remarks about the Armenian genocide.

events.title: The Gezi Park protests
events.description: A sit-in against a shopping mall in central Istanbul grows into nationwide protests and is cleared by force.

events.title: The failed coup
events.description: A faction of the army bombs parliament and seizes the Bosphorus bridges overnight. Crowds stop them, about 250 die, and some 150,000 people are later purged.

events.title: A presidential system
events.description: A referendum narrowly abolishes the post of prime minister and concentrates executive power in the presidency.

events.title: Hagia Sophia is a mosque again
events.description: A court annuls the 1934 decision that made it a museum, and Friday prayers are held under the dome.

events.title: The Kahramanmaras earthquakes
events.description: Two earthquakes hours apart kill over fifty thousand people in Turkey and thousands more in Syria, the deadliest disaster in the republic's history.
